question: What Is the Working Principle of an Induction Generator?
body_html:
An induction generator is an induction machine whose rotor is driven above synchronous speed, so slip turns negative, rotor currents reverse and active power flows out of the stator. It still draws reactive power from the grid or capacitors to build its field.

Ns = 120 × f ÷ P and s = (Ns − N) ÷ Ns. Example: a 4 pole machine on 50 Hz has Ns = 1500 rpm; at 1530 rpm, s = −0.02, so it generates.
